sentence_of_record: BOUNDARY-DISAGREEMENT (2026-09-17, zero calls): on the merged board of record (21,519 matches, 2,808 questions) the lowest-margin quintile shows no excess of ties (-0.2pp [-2.4, +2.1]) or order flips (+0.4pp [-1.3, +2.1]) over the highest, and the leaf-FE within-cell flip coefficient is -0.024 [-0.074, +0.025] (C1 FAILED, C2 FAILED, C3 HELD no difference, C4 NOT SHOWN); the registered falsifier fires through C2, so no dual-cell arm is launched and MULTI-OWNERSHIP as a judging mechanism closes at zero calls. Qualifiers of record: (i) the merged null averages two schedules that disagree on the same 2,643 questions: the x12 66-pair schedule reads flip +2.9pp [+0.4, +5.4] (C1 flip HELD; anchor-FE -0.086 [-0.155, -0.016]; within-anchor standardised tie +3.5pp [+0.3, +6.8], flip +3.8pp [+1.1, +6.5]) and the x20 124-novel-pair schedule -1.2pp [-3.6, +1.1] (leaf-FE +0.002), paired difference +4.2pp [+1.0, +7.5]; (ii) C2 has no power clause and its merged interval contains -0.057, the coefficient a 2pp flip gap would produce, so the mechanism is not shown rather than shown absent; (iii) the raw quintile contrast is anchor-confounded (Q1/Q5: Psychology 78/7, Law 27/124) and Q1 questions are easier on the key (0.563 vs 0.488), so difficulty does not account for the x12 signal; (iv) the depth-1 secondary margin reads positive on merged (tie +2.5 [+0.3, +4.6], flip +2.5 [+0.7, +4.3]) and wrong(established) B +4.8pp [+1.7, +8.1] on x20 alone, anchor-confounded (Q5 one-third Law), an unregistered lead only; (v) under STACK-v2 the only cell-dependence is the anchor rubric and 225 of the 314 router two-candidate questions have both candidates in one anchor, so a dual-cell arm would post the identical prompt on 72% of its targets; multi-ownership as an attribution or reporting choice (a question contributing to two cells' boards) was not tested and remains open. plain_description.what: No judge calls. On about 21,500 existing judged matches, the test compared questions that sit near a cell boundary (low routing margin) with questions deep inside a cell. It looked for more ties, more verdicts that flip when the answer order is swapped, and less stable model rankings.
plain_description.why: It checks the idea behind 'multi-ownership' (judging boundary questions in two cells): that the judge struggles most at cell boundaries.
plain_description.information: An excess of disagreement at boundaries would justify a paid dual-cell judging run. No excess would close that idea for free. Result: done. On the merged board there was no clear excess of ties or flips, so no dual-cell run was launched and the idea closes as a judging mechanism. Qualifier: on one of the two schedules (x12) flips were somewhat higher at boundaries, so the mechanism is 'not shown', not shown to be absent. Note: this record belongs to the older question pool, which the author ruled 'history, not evidence'.
